Arriving at the &rtber bank at the Bhagirathi, Labbmana, 
with joined palms, his &ce bathed in tears, said :-
"A stake has been driven into my heart by the noble and 
virtuous Rama, which will bring universal censure upon me. 
Death were better for me this day, verily death would be 
preferable to the mission on which I am engaged, which the 
world will condemn. 
Forgive me and do not impute this 
offence to me, 0 Illustrious Princess." 
Thereafter, making obeisance, Labhmana threw himself on 
the earth. Seeing him weep, paying her homage and calling on 
death, Maithili, alarmed, said to Labhmana :-
" What is this ? I do not understand anything ; tell me the 
truth, 0 Labhmana, why att thou agitated ? Is the king well ? 
Tell me the cause at thy grief!" 
Thus questioned by Vaidehi, Labhmana, his heart filled 
with anguish, with bowed head, choked with sobs, addressed 
her saying :-
" Having learnt in open council that he was the object of 
sevete censure in the city and country on thine account, 0 
Daughter of Janab, Rama, his heart riven, returning home told 
me of it. I am unable to repeat the things spoken in confidence 
to me, 0 Queen. Although thou att blameless in mine eyes, 
the king has repudiated thee. Public condemnation has per-
turbed him; do not misunderstand the matter, 0 Goddess. I 
am to leave thee in the vicinity of the sacred hermitages. The 
king has commanded me to do so on the pretext of satisfying thy 
desire. The ascetics' retreats on the banks of the Jahnavi are 
sacred and enchanting, do not give way to grief, 0 Lovely One. 
The foremost of Rishis, the supretncly illustrious Sage Valmild 
was a great friend of thy sire, King Dasaratha. Taking refuge 
under the shadow at the feet of that magnanimous One and 
living in chastity, be happy, 0 Daughter at Janab. It is by 
remaining filithful to thy Lord and practising devotion to Rama 
in thine heart that thou shalt, by thy conduct, acquire supreme 
felicity, 0 Goddess."

brief.summary_1line: Lakshmana tearfully reveals that Rama, fearing public scandal, has ordered Sita abandoned near the hermitages by the Ganges.

image_candidates.scene_text: On the quiet bank of the Ganges, Lakshmana falls to the ground in tears before the bewildered Sita after bringing her across the river.
Lakshmana, hands folded and face wet with tears, stands before Sita on the forested riverbank as he confesses Rama has repudiated her.
A small boat drifts across the wide Ganges at noon carrying Sita and the grief‑stricken Lakshmana toward the lonely forest shore.

deep.rich_summary: Sita, Lakshmana, and the charioteer Sumantra reach the sacred Ganges during what Sita believes is a brief pilgrimage to visit sages and distribute gifts. Lakshmana, however, is overwhelmed with grief. After ferrying Sita across the Bhagirathi, he finally reveals the truth: Rama has heard public gossip questioning Sita’s purity despite her earlier trial by fire. Though Lakshmana insists she is blameless, Rama fears public condemnation and has ordered that she be left near the hermitages along the river. Lakshmana begs forgiveness for carrying out the command. The scene marks one of the most tragic turns of the Ramayana—Sita’s abandonment while pregnant and the painful conflict between royal duty, public opinion, and personal loyalty.

highlight_spans.why: Sita joyfully speaks of crossing the Ganges and visiting sages, unaware of Lakshmana’s hidden mission, heightening the tragic irony.
Lakshmana breaks down, saying a stake has been driven into his heart and that death would be preferable to his task.
The crucial revelation: Lakshmana explains that Rama has heard public censure and has repudiated Sita despite her innocence.
Lakshmana directs Sita toward the hermitages near the Ganges and the protection of the sage Valmiki, foreshadowing the next phase of her life.

top_scenes.scene_text: Lakshmana stands on the lonely bank of the Ganges with folded hands and tear-filled eyes as Sita looks at him in confusion beside the waiting boat.
On the far bank of the Bhagirathi, Lakshmana collapses to the ground in anguish before Sita as he reveals Rama’s command to abandon her.
The small boat glides across the vast sacred Ganges at noon, with a grieving Lakshmana silently rowing while the unsuspecting Sita gazes at the shining river.
